key_facts: ASUS는 **8개 Rubin GPU를 탑재한 HGX Rubin NVL8** 액체냉각 솔루션을 전시했으며, GPU 방향을 뒤집는 새 보드 설계로 효율적 액체냉각을 구현했다
NVIDIA는 신세대 **NVLink Switch**를 온보드에 탑재하고 고속 스케일아웃 네트워킹으로 대형 클러스터 구성을 지원한다
새 설계는 8개 GPU를 공랭 시 6U 이상 필요했던 것을 **1U에 집적**해 랙 밀도를 크게 높였다
ASUS는 GB200/GB300 NVL72 및 Vera Rubin NVL72 기반 ORv3 트레이를 'ASUS AI Pod'로 명명해 전시했다
Vera Rubin NVL72는 섀시 내 팬을 제거하고 랙 전체를 액체냉각하는 방향으로 발전, 전력당 컴퓨트 밀도를 극대화한다

cards.body: Recently, I was in Seoul, South Korea, for the ASUS AI Tech 2026 event. This is ASUS’s event where it showcases its new AI servers, racks, and offerings, along with its suppliers, partners, and customers. At the event, I moderated a panel discussion, so I thought it was worth an article and a short video. Of course, ASUS paid for my travel, so we have to say this is sponsored. ASUS AI Tech 2026 Seoul, South Korea In the lobby, there were all kinds of AI servers. That included NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 solutions with eight Rubin GPUs. ASUS showed off a number of these, including an awesome-looking liquid-cooled version that is a massive change from Ampere, Hopper, and Blackwell generation designs. This generation flips the GPU orientation on the baseboard to enable more efficient liquid cooling. NVIDIA also brings a new generation of NVLink Switch onboard, with high-speed scale-out NVIDIA networking to enable larger clusters. This design also lets the eight GPUs fit in 1U instead of taking 6U or more to air-cool the HGX baseboard, making them much denser. ASUS uses this plus another chassis segment for the CPUs, SSDs, DPUs, and more to fit a huge amount of compute into much denser rack footprints than we have seen previously. The ability to use either hybrid cooling or all-liquid cooling in these nodes helps them fit into data centers with different capabilities. While the individual GPUs may use more power than a Hopper-generation GPU, for example, the higher-performance Rubin GPUs mean that the onboard NVL8 topology has more compute resources and memory connected, minimizing data movement. In turn, that means that not only is each GPU faster, but the NVL8 domain is significantly faster and can hold more data, so that way more communication can stay within the node instead of having to go out to the scale-out fabric. ASUS also brought trays from its NVIDIA GB200/GB300 NVL72 and Vera Rubin NVL72 solutions that it calls the ASUS AI Pod. It was neat seeing the different liquid-cooled ORv3 trays on the floor. The all-liquid-cooled design increases efficiency, which ultimately determines how much performance you can get from a data center. That was a key theme among the day’s speakers. You could also see the generational shift toward moving fans out of the chassis and liquid-cooling everything in the rack in the newer Vera Rubin NVL72 design. That helps increase compute density and maximize performance within a given power footprint. We previously showed you how they are tested in our ASUS Thermal Lab Tour 2026 Testing AI Servers. If you want to check that out, you can find the short video for that one here: Next, let us get to the storage and our panel discussion.

summary_data.why_matters: AI 데이터센터의 급증하는 발열 문제 해결을 위해 엔비디아가 냉각 파트너 생태계를 공식화하면서, **엔비디아 인증 냉각 솔루션**이 AI 인프라 구축의 표준 검토 대상으로 자리잡게 된다. 이는 GPU 성능 확장과 직결된 열관리 병목 해소를 위해 하드웨어 파트너 생태계를 확장하려는 엔비디아 전략의 일환이다.
summary_data.subject_angle: 엔비디아는 자사 GPU 기반 AI 팩토리의 전력·냉각 인프라를 표준화·인증함으로써 **하드웨어 생태계 전반을 락인**하고, 고객사들이 검증된 파트너 솔루션을 통해 대규모 GPU 클러스터를 안정적으로 도입하도록 유도한다.

cards.body: LG전자가 엔비디아의 공식 파트너 프로그램인 ‘엔비디아 파트너 네트워크(NPN)’의 전력·냉각 분야 파트너로 정식 등재됐다고 27일 밝혔다. NPN은 엔비디아의 AI 컴퓨팅 생태계를 기반으로 하드웨어, 인프라 등 관련 기업들이 참여하는 글로벌 협력 프로그램이다. 이번 파트너 등재로 LG전자는 엔비디아 기술 기반 AI 데이터센터를 구축하는 글로벌 고객사들과의 접점을 넓히게 됐다. 회사 측은 초기 기획 및 설계 단계부터 LG전자의 칠러·냉각수 분배장치(CDU) 등 고효율 냉각 솔루션이 도입 후보로 검토될 가능성이 높아질 것으로 기대하고 있다. 앞서 LG전자는 국내 기업 최초로 600킬로와트(kW) 및 1메가와트(MW)급 CDU에 대해 엔비디아 규격 승인 요건을 충족했다. 고용량인 2.5MW급 CDU 역시 AI 팩토리 규격 승인을 받아 엔비디아 인증 제품으로 등재되는 등 기술적 요건을 정식 인정받았다. LG전자는 2011년 데이터센터 냉각 시장에 진출한 이후 대형 칠러 제품을 기반으로 사업을 확대해 왔다. 최근에는 고발열 AI 서버용 칩셋을 직접 식히는 액체냉각 솔루션까지 확보하며 칠러부터 CDU, 콜드 플레이트에 이르는 ‘칩 투 칠러’ 냉각 풀 라인업을 구축했다. 회사는 이번 파트너십을 계기로 신규 데이터센터 증설 수요의 60% 이상이 집중된 북미 시장을 비롯해 초대형 클라우드 기업, 임대형 데이터센터 시장 공략을 강화할 계획이다. 천선우 기자 swchun@chosunbiz.com

headlines.body: Hi all, long-time lurker finally posting. Background: I recently finished building a 4x DGX Spark cluster serving DeepSeek V4.1 Flash locally (the new 552B MoE — the DCE architecture's KV cache compression makes it surprisingly light to run). It's been a fun project and the setup works great. Now I'm in the early research phase for a GPU upgrade and trying to understand the global market landscape. In China, availability and pricing for the RTX PRO 6000 (96GB Blackwell) has been quite volatile, which got me curious: How does its pricing compare to MSRP in your region? Is stock easy to find locally, or still constrained? For those who've built mixed setups — how do you find the PRO 6000 pairs with unified-memory boxes like the Spark? Also happy to chat about the China side of things — the local LLM scene, GLM/Kimi and other services, or what the hardware market looks like here. Always interesting to compare notes across regions. Cheers from Shanghai! submitted by /u/PassionVegetable3431 [link] [comments]

related.title: Thieves steal Nvidia-labeled trailers – yields 20 tons of sand

headlines.body: PlusAI, an autonomous trucking startup, is working with Nvidia to develop its systems and has several trucks and trailers marked with the logos of both companies. This likely caught the attention of thieves who were looking to score big on AI GPUs, with Wired reporting that two of the startup’s trailers got stolen and were found at another location. However, the joke’s on the criminals, as they discovered that the two stolen units contained 20,000 pounds of sand each. The AI data center construction boom has made PC components like RAM and GPUs insanely expensive, which has led to a rise in petty theft involving these components. Enterprises and startups are being targeted, too, especially as they build data centers and local AI servers with millions of dollars’ worth of equipment and hardware. We’ve already seen cargo heists of copper cable and other hardware worth $1.3 million , while other criminals have become more brazen, pushing or spinning security escorts off the road so they can get away with a truck’s worth of AI GPUs. While PlusAI is partnered with Nvidia, it also uses simulated cargo loads for real-world tests, allowing the company to model how a fully loaded semi-trailer would react to various road conditions. The startup’s truck cabs, which likely had advanced AI hardware installed, were parked securely inside its warehouse, while the trailers were apparently left outside and secured with hand locks. “PlusAI uses simulated loads in its trailers to assist with research and development testing,” company spokesperson Lauren Kwan told Wired, adding that they were recovered with “40,000 pounds of sand intact.” Interestingly, the discovery of the theft was accidentally made by one of the startup’s top executives, who received a message from an acquaintance saying that they saw the trailers, which they described as “trucks,” near their workplace. This likely got the executive concerned, as that location was half a mile away from PlusAI’s warehouse, which led to the cops getting called. As for the prospective criminals, they probably left the crime scene disappointed — they thought they were getting a huge payday from two truckloads’ worth of smart silicon, but they ended up with 20 tons of dumb sand instead.
